answer:
VAEs offer fast amortized encoding and typically fast decoding with a likelihood lower bound, but likelihood/objective and decoder choices can trade detail for coverage. GANs often sample sharply in one generator pass but can miss modes and are difficult to train. Normalizing flows provide exact likelihood and invertible maps, with architectural constraints and speed depending on the flow. Diffusion models often combine strong quality and diversity at the cost of iterative sampling. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6114) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.00028) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239)

These are tendencies, not an impossibility theorem with a fixed winner. Distilled diffusion, consistency-style methods, latent representations, and autoregressive or continuous flows shift the frontier. Compare matched data, compute, resolution, quality/coverage metrics, and end-to-end latency. High perceptual quality is not synonymous with calibrated likelihood or complete mode coverage.
